To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Thursday launch handover for Inês

DRAFT — for me to read before sharing

Inês,

I have to leave tonight because my father is ill and I am with my family. I don’t know yet how long I’ll be away, so please plan to lead Thursday’s launch without me.

I am sorry to hand this over at such short notice, especially with a correction still to get out. The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours. You should say that if anyone asks; you do not need to absorb it on my behalf.

I trust you completely. You know this paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity work yourself. You are not standing in to read someone else’s argument: this is your work too. Below is the order I think things need to happen in, with the outstanding decisions separated from what is already settled.

1. First: get the correction under control

The correct estimate for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. Figure 3 and the summary had carried over the estimate from the old run, which did not apply the free-allocation phase-out.

The paper’s conclusion does not change, but the headline number does. We should be straightforward about both parts of that.

PDF v7 on the drive is already corrected on pages 3, 14 and 15. Please use that as the master version and check that it is the version used for any launch distribution or publication.

Still to fix:
- Deck v4: slides 6 and 9. Slide 9 contains the revenue chart. Please check the speaker notes too, since my old notes are still in the deck, and look for any other references to 2.1.
- The embargoed press release Hanna sent on Friday to 34 Brussels contacts. That still says 2.1.

Please contact Hanna first, rather than waiting until the deck is finished. She needs to send a clearly marked correction to everyone who received the original release, with the corrected release and PDF v7, before the embargo lifts on Thursday 26 November at 10:00 CET. Ask her to make clear that the earlier 2.1 figure should not be used. We should not rely on journalists noticing a replacement attachment.

Geert knows I am away. If Hanna needs a senior name to sign off the corrected release, he can do that. Please take that route rather than letting my availability hold things up.

A line you can use, including for the press calls:

“We corrected an error in the 2030 revenue estimate: the correct figure is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The earlier figure came from a run that did not apply the free-allocation phase-out. The headline estimate changes; the paper’s conclusion does not.”

If asked who made the mistake: it was mine. There is no need to soften that or explain my circumstances.

2. Next: agree the revised event plan with Tomás

The run-of-show document from Friday is no longer the latest timing. Tomás emailed today because Lindqvist now has to leave at 13:30.

His requested changes are:
- Presentation reduced from 20 minutes to 15.
- Panel starts at 12:50, not 12:55.
- Lindqvist would like to take at least two questions herself before leaving.

Please tell Tomás you will present and take my panel place, and confirm the revised arrangements with him. The moderator arrangements after 13:30 still need agreeing: the old schedule has Q&A at 13:40, which plainly does not cover her request for questions before she goes. Please settle where those questions fit and who takes over moderation when she leaves. Don’t assume that part has been sorted.

The working outline is therefore:
- 12:00: guests at the security entrance; Tomás collects badges. Light lunch outside the room from 12:00.
- 12:30: Lindqvist’s welcome, five minutes.
- 12:35: your presentation, 15 minutes.
- 12:50: panel with you, Abena and Kessler.
- Before 13:30: at least two audience questions with Lindqvist, placement to confirm.
- 13:30 onwards: moderation and remaining discussion/Q&A to confirm.
- 14:00: close, unless Tomás advises otherwise.

Venue is the European Parliament, Altiero Spinelli building, in the room booked by Lindqvist’s office.

The hard deadline here is Wednesday 25 November at 12:00: Tomás needs final names of everyone attending from our side for security. Please send the list by then and make sure it reflects the change of presenter. Without the names, people will not get in.

3. Tomorrow/Wednesday: press calls and presentation

Hanna promised two journalists a background call with me on Wednesday afternoon: one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. The calendar has Wednesday 25 November at 14:00 and 15:00, 20 minutes each, but both are marked “Hanna to confirm”.

Please ask Hanna to confirm the callers and timings and arrange who will take them. If you can do them, I would be very happy for you to; if that creates too much pressure alongside the launch, work out another arrangement with her. Either way, they need to hear about the correction before the conversation gets into the findings. They should not be left expecting a call from me.

For the presentation, use the corrected deck and cut to 15 minutes. You know better than I do which transitions you can make quickly. Keep enough time to explain the revenue finding and what we recommend; don’t let the shorter slot turn into a rushed tour of all 14 slides.

Abena’s remote link is in the calendar invite. In your deck notes you said she had tested it and it worked. Please let her know you are taking over and check the connection and room arrangements again before the event. A successful earlier test is helpful, but I would still want a launch-day check.

4. On the panel: be open about the sensitivities, then move on

Kessler has already said he will raise the 80% downstream steel-user pass-through assumption and resource shuffling. He is likely to try to make the whole discussion about the 80%. Don’t let him set the tone.

The honest answer on pass-through is:
- 80% is the central case.
- Annex B tests 60% and 40%.
- The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%.

Say that openly, without becoming defensive or claiming the result is equally strong in every case. You ran those tests. You can explain what they show and where the limits are, then bring the discussion back to the paper’s question about CBAM revenues and least developed countries. You do not have to spend the entire panel defending a single assumption.

On resource shuffling, we agree it is a risk. Section 5.2 addresses it, and we recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. Acknowledge the point rather than treating it as something we missed.

Abena was strong on the LDC side in our call and may help keep that perspective in the discussion. Give her room to make her own argument; don’t count on her to defend ours.

And please remember Lisbon. When the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel without making anyone feel there had been a rescue. You are better live than you think. If Thursday goes off-script, I trust your judgement much more than I trust any set of notes I could leave.

5. Small but important follow-through

Lucy Tran from Halvorsen is attending with a colleague. She needs two event photos and attendance numbers for the grant report, ideally by 4 December. Please arrange in advance who will take the photos and who will record attendance, so this does not become another thing you have to remember while presenting.

After the launch, please make sure the corrected PDF and final deck are the versions kept for follow-up, and that Hanna has what she needs for any journalist queries about the number.

Availability and what to say about my absence

You can call me. After 09:00 tomorrow, Tuesday, I might not pick up, so please don’t build any deadline around reaching me. For the corrected release, use Geert if senior sign-off is needed. For the presentation and discussion, you have my full confidence to make the calls.

If anyone asks about me, please keep it to: “My father is ill, I am with my family.” Nothing more is needed.

I am sorry about the mess and about leaving you to carry this at the last minute. I don’t take that lightly. But I am not worried about whether you can do it. I trust you completely, and I want you to feel free to lead it in your own way, not spend Thursday trying to be me.

Marieke
